author: EmuCore - Hub
title: AetherSX2 - Playstation 2 Emulator for Android (4 Games Test) (SD845) - Part 2
summary: Emulation Galaxy compares early AetherSX2 builds 669 and 678 on a Snapdragon 845 Galaxy S9+, combining four long game samples with a first-hand warning that emulator updates cost two memory-card folders.

blocks.text: The thirty-six-minute recording preserves more continuity than a standard benchmark: Yu Yu Hakusho Forever receives almost eleven minutes, followed by God Hand, Clock Tower 3 and Fatal Frame. The host is a Snapdragon 845 Galaxy S9+ on Android 10, capture uses Samsung’s built-in recorder and input comes from an Ipega 9087. Two games run at 2x scale. Most importantly, the creator identifies builds 669 and 678 and reports a performance drop after the first package.

The lost-memory-card warning is stronger than the performance claim: early emulator updates can invalidate assumptions about storage, so saves need external versioned backups before any build change. The notes do not give settings for every game, temperatures, frame-time graphs, exact disc regions or the cause of the two losses. Google Play early-access links are now historical. Use the footage to study long scenes on Snapdragon 845 and to justify backup discipline, not to install obsolete packages or assign regressions without a matched build comparison.
